title and abstract.summary: The study measured the relationship between functional traits (body size, phenology, nesting location, sociality, and foraging choice) and the prevalence of trypanosomes, neogregarines, and Nosema ceranae in wild bee communities, and also evaluated intra-specific size variation in Bombus impatiens. The study investigates how functional traits, such as body size and phenology, might influence pathogen prevalence in bee communities, using Bombus impatiens as an example. The study measured the effect of initial pathogen prevalence on final prevalence in colonies of Bombus impatiens, Apis mellifer
